task: Escribe 90–110 palabras sobre tu forma de comprar ropa: ¿compras de segunda mano? ¿Qué harías para consumir menos? Usa comparativos y al menos un condicional.
paragraphs: Not long ago, wearing second-hand clothes was something many people did only when they had no money. Today it has become fashionable. Apps for selling used clothes have millions of users, and vintage shops are full of young customers looking for something different.

One reason is the price. A designer jacket that costs hundreds of pounds when it is new can be found for a fraction of that online. But money is not the only motivation. Many shoppers say they are worried about the environment.

The fashion industry has a serious impact on the planet. Producing new clothes uses huge amounts of water and energy, and many garments are made from synthetic materials that come from oil. "Fast fashion" brands produce new collections every few weeks, at very low prices, so people buy more and throw away more. Every year, millions of tonnes of clothes end up in landfills or are burned.

Buying second-hand helps, because it makes clothes last longer. If a T-shirt is worn by two people instead of one, fewer new T-shirts need to be made. Some people go further and organise swap parties, where friends exchange clothes they no longer wear.

Not everyone is enthusiastic, though. Some critics point out that people who buy cheap second-hand clothes online often buy more than they need, so they don't really consume less. Others worry that charity shops, which used to sell cheap clothes to people on low incomes, are now more expensive because of the demand.
Still, for many young people, a second-hand wardrobe is a way of showing their values. As one student put it: "I like knowing that my favourite coat already has a story."
